description: Make the factory session registry the sole source of truth for live runtimes: register ~default like other sessions, route reads and activation through session handles, share one runtime bundle type, and remove authoritative shadow runtime fields from FactoryService without changing API or session semantics.

context.customerAsk: Session registry as sole runtime truth; drop duplicate FactoryService fields. Full spec: tasks/prd-service-runtime-state-consolidation.md
context.problem: FactoryService still mirrors the active runtime in top-level fields while multi-session work already lives in factorysessions.Registry handles. That duplication lets work submit, factory save, snapshots, and idle checks target the wrong session or update the service root when a non-default session is active.
context.solution: Incrementally route all runtime access through the session registry and liveRuntimeHandle, unify activation on replaceSessionRuntime, collapse build and live bundle types, then remove authoritative top-level runtime fields while preserving API, CLI, and session open/close behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: Every live runtime including ~default is registered in factorysessions.Registry with a liveRuntimeHandle; production code does not treat top-level FactoryService runtime fields as authoritative.
Work submission, engine snapshots, events, and idle checks scoped by session_id observe only that session's factory and artifacts; concurrent multi-session isolation is preserved.
Runtime replacement after persist uses session-scoped activation and writes the current-factory pointer under the targeted session root.
Process restart restores only ~default; additional live sessions remain ephemeral with no behavior change from today.
No OpenAPI request or response shape changes.
Typecheck, lint, and project tests pass.

userStories.title: One runtime bundle shape for build and live handles
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a single runtime bundle type so build output and live session handles cannot drift when runtime wiring grows.
acceptanceCriteria: Building a runtime for service startup or session open returns one shared bundle type carrying factory, net, listener, loaded config, logger, event history, local models, recording, and related sidecars.
liveRuntimeHandle references that shared type; adding a new runtime sidecar requires updating one struct definition.
Existing service build and replay tests that start a runtime continue to pass without relaxed assertions.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Default session lives in the registry at startup
userStories.description: As an operator running a single factory, I want the default session registered the same way as named sessions so session targeting is uniform from the first request.
acceptanceCriteria: After BuildFactoryService and service run, ~default is present in the session registry with a live handle pointing at the started factory directory.
Default session registration uses the same registerLiveSession path as OpenFactorySession, not a parallel service-only runtime slot.
runState.sessionID matches the registry entry used for ~default while the default runtime is active.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Runtime operations target the requested session
userStories.description: As a dashboard user with multiple factory tabs, I want work, snapshots, and idle checks for each session_id to use only that session's runtime so sessions cannot leak into one another.
acceptanceCriteria: Submitting work to session A records artifacts and dispatch identifiers only for session A; session B's replay and log artifacts do not contain session A work.
Engine snapshot and factory read APIs scoped by session_id return data from that session's factory directory, not another live session's directory.
Idle checks used before factory activation apply to the session being saved or opened, not whichever session was selected last on the service root.
pkg/api session-scoped routing tests continue to pass: mutations and reads for session-beta do not invoke default-session factories.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Runtime replacement is always session-scoped
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want every runtime swap after persist to stop the prior handle for the same session and start the replacement under that session's root.
acceptanceCriteria: Factory definition save, OpenFactorySession, and named-factory activation call replaceSessionRuntime with the session idle guard, not the legacy global activation entry point.
When replacing the factory for a non-default session, the current-factory pointer is written under that session's SessionFactoryRootDir, not only the service host root.
A successful replacement stops the previous live handle for the same session before registering the successor; other live sessions keep running.
Service-mode sidecar start and stop behavior is unchanged (poller, cron, and related service tests still pass).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: FactoryService no longer mirrors live runtime state
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want FactoryService to hold wiring and session orchestration only, so there is one obvious place to find the live runtime for a session.
acceptanceCriteria: Top-level factory, net, listener, runtimeCfg, and related runtime fields are removed or reduced to thin delegators that read the selected or requested session handle.
Runtime swap for a session updates only that session's registry entry and runState for that session; no production path writes the same swap to both top-level fields and the session handle.
Default and named-session behavior for submit, pause, wait-for-complete, and model catalog APIs remains unchanged from the caller's perspective.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Restart behavior documented for operators
userStories.description: As an operator running multiple UI tabs, I need clear documentation of which sessions survive a process restart so I do not assume ephemeral tabs are restored.
acceptanceCriteria: Internal maintainer documentation states that only ~default is restored when the service process restarts; additional live sessions opened before restart are ephemeral and must be reopened.
TestFactoryService_Run_RestartsOnlyDefaultSession continues to pass without changing expected session count or default runtime directory after restart.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
